pr_title: Fix: InputEventJoypadMotion should trigger only once on a vslider
pr_body:
Fixes #62932
Closes https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/4911

Both slider and popup_menu has been modified to support joypad motion.

https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1162446/217901269-05cfddb6-b205-49a2-be84-398d1be1d2b4.mp4
pr_comments: It could also be backported to 3.x. Was tested on both 4.0, 3.4 and 3.5
PR has been updated to match my proposal https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/4911

I suggest renaming `default_slider_repeating_rate` to `default_joypad_motion_repeating_rate` 
and `default_slider_delay_timer`to `default_joypad_motion_delay_timer` ,
and apply these changes to all control nodes that change UI focus/behavior in their `_gui_input`. 
They are `ItemList`, `PopupMenu`, `RichTextLabel`, `ScrollBar`, `Slider` and `Tree`. I'm not sure if `CodeEdit` needs this, maybe also yes?
Then it will fix #71918, #35751, and other issues that I have not found or have not yet raised.

It should also be applied to Viewport to make UI focus change with common control nodes benefit too.

@univeous I updated my PR to add slider, pop_menu, item_list, tree and rich text label.

But I'm pretty much stock about the Viewport. I'm pretty confuse about how the viewport manage the focus and pass it to the selected node. It seems to conflict with the timer and node position.

It also create some issue with item_list and tree. If I focus out and re-focus on the item, echoing and the whole direction with the gamepad broke. A quick workaround could be simply to ignore those control and only applied the fix on slider, popup_menu and rich text label.

https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1162446/216380927-8c585de7-8639-463c-b64e-f65243d64754.mp4
https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1162446/216381030-cf164a78-a339-4852-9a88-6fbd5d79449a.mp4

I also saw the following issue, if we focus on a rich_text_label, we can't focus out (both keyboard and gamepad). I will create an issue for that.

The test project can be download right here https://github.com/Levrault/joypad-motion-echo

Sorry I haven't gone through your implementation in detail, but I feel that instead of implementing similar logic in every gui node, it might be better to implement a helper function in the Input class somehow, or implement echo event for joypad motion input. It might be harder to implement though. 
Maybe we should call more people to join the conversation. CC @groud @EricEzaM

First of all, thanks for working on that!

I don't feel like the implementation is right though. Echo events aren't really meant for handling, like, "continuous pressing" of a given key. TBH, I don't think echo events are very useful nowadays. They kind of make sense for moving a text cursor, for, like, compatibility with the fact the OS asks us to handle the event. However,  they could also be very easily replaced by a check to `is_action_pressed(...)` in the `process` function (in our situation), which in general provide a lot more customizable behavior than relying on how often, and after which delay, the OS sends us the echo events.

As a consequence, I don't think that this implementation is perfect, as i don't think it should emulate echo events out of joypad events. It makes things more complex than things need to be, and creates an additional constraint for little gain. Instead, I believe each control should check themselves the status of each ui_left/right... actions in their `process` function. It might make use of some helper function if you need to, though I am not sure it's needed. Overall it would likely simplify the implementation by avoiding to rely on those crafted fake events.

@groud  checking `Input.is_action_pressed` in the `_process` function seems way more cleaner but delay and repeat reate should be keep in some specific case scenario like the slider.

e.g.
```
Slider: Min value is 0, max value is 100, the value is increment by 5 each times. The default value is 100.

1- The user move his left joystick to the left
2- `gui_input` catch the input and decrement the value to 95
3- The user keep his left joystick to the left
4- After 20 frames, we decrement the value to 90 
5- The user keep his left joystick to the left
6 - After 10 frames, we decrement the value to 85, 80 until the user stop using the left joystick.
```
This is the default slider behavior in many games and we should tried to archieve it. I also think supporting it out-of-the-box should be great for the user like @BlooRabbit said in https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/71918#issuecomment-1416416679 and https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/62932

But others controls like the popup_menu, item list, tree, could only have simple repeat rate. We re-call the gui_input function every X frames to seems if the Input is still pressed. And incremental repeat rate doesn't seems necessary for those nodes.

I just need some leads about how it should be implemented. Instead of timer, I think and repeat rate at each X frames could be cleaner. Maybe directly re-calling `gui_input` in the process function could be cleaner and prevent code duplication, but I don't know if it's possible. 

Also having a more contextual incremental behavior by control could be the best way to help our user and their futurs users.

> I just need some leads about how it should be implemented. Instead of timer, I think and repeat rate at each X frames could be cleaner.

Input repeat speed should not depend on rendering or physics FPS, as it will feel wildly inconsistent on games running at varying framerates (and possibly way too fast at uncapped framerates). Physics FPS may also be changed by the developer in the project settings or at run-time, and it shouldn't have side effects on UI.

You should keep using some form of timer, even if it's just a check against a stored ticks value in microseconds (`OS::get_singleton()->get_ticks_usec()`).

> @groud checking Input.is_action_pressed in the _process function seems way more cleaner but delay and repeat reate should be keep in some specific case scenario like the slider.

Yeah you are right. The way it can be implemented is not that complex though:
- In the gui_input handler, handle the event like it used to be before (a single time, with a predetermined step value).
- In the process function, start some sort of a timer (that resets when you are not pressing the action). Then, after a given delay, move the slider by `step_value * delta * step_per_second_factor`. 

The timer does not need to be a Timer node/scene tree Timer btw, you can just store a "started pressing" time and check the difference with the current time. It would be lighter than using a node. (Edit: ah, just realized that's what Calinou suggested.)
Not sure if enabling process for many GUI nodes is a good idea (unless they have that already?). It should probably get enabled with key press and disabled with release.

@groud and @Calinou I updated my PR with the new approach. It's still far from perfect. I wanted to call `gui_input`inside `_notification` to prevent code duplication but I didn't found any usefull function that would return a `Ref<InputEvent>` for a specific action. I also ended up using `get_process_delta_time` instead of `OS::get_singleton()->get_ticks_usec()`. 

@KoBeWi set_process is activated only when a the gamepad motion is used. I don't know if this could interfer if an user use _process for something specific.

> I don't know if this could interfer if an user use _process for something specific.

This should use internal process, to not interfere with user code.

idk if it's just me or the movement has a weird jitter 🤔

https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/2223172/232902010-135aa8ac-cc49-4db5-a376-1270af53c6bb.mp4
Seems fine, but I left some comments. The comments I left in PopupMenu also apply to Slider (mostly).

@KoBeWi The same jitter seems to happen when using the keyboard :/ it seems left visible since it's a little bit faster the gamepad


https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1162446/233099122-49d703fe-456b-46e7-acd6-851d79b27f68.mp4

Thanks! And congrats for your first merged Godot contribution :tada:

issue_context.title: InputEventJoypadMotion will trigger multiples on_value_changed with hslider
issue_context.body:
### Godot version

3.4.4 (and 3.3.4, 3.5-rc6)

### System information

Windows 10

### Issue description

Hi all, 
If you map `ui_left `and `ui_left` with the left joystick of a controller (xbox one in this case), when using a hslider, the on changed value event will be trigged multiples times. 

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1162446/178392628-b6b1ceb7-fd87-472e-bc6c-8381ff1dd071.png)

e.g. a hslider with a step of 5%, with the stick, the value increase randomly from 10% to 20%, while using the direction cross will only trigger a 5% step.

https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1162446/178392471-b41b5954-1482-45d8-adf1-8ad2027e1635.mp4

I think InputEventJoypadMotion should only be trigger once to match industry standard.

If this isn't a duplicate, I would be interested to take a look and create a PR if this is a good "first issue".

Thanks

### Steps to reproduce

1 - Create a minimal project with a hslider
2 - Remap ui_left, ui_right to the left joystick
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1162446/178392854-69af922a-49bc-47cf-b76c-6a6080380268.png)
3 - Create a hslider
4 - Change the value with the joystick

### Minimal reproduction project

[hslider_issue.zip](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/files/9088786/hslider_issue.zip)
comments: Reproduced with a XBox One controller via USB on 3.x custom build. Doesn't seem like a "controller drift" problem
Up-to-date one, last commit in log is 3f02013
@Calinou hi, I wrote the wrong version (I tested both on 3.3.4, 3.4.4, 3.5-rc6), same behaviour on both version

Same with 4.0 alpha 10.

I think the problem isn't with the code for controller but how the slider reacts to stick's inputs.
If you push the stick to left/right and do not release, the slider will stop at some position (may have moved more than once), but sometimes when you release it, it will move again in the same direction.

So in this case, I think the desirable behaviour should be to detect delta is the same direction as previously received one, and therefore the slider should not react to it, and when inside the deadzone, consider it as released.

Slider inputs will likely need special handling to behave well with InputEventJoypadMotion. InputEventJoypadMotion should not be ignored by Slider; otherwise, you would only be able to use the D-pad to move a slider (which is poor UX).

You'll likely need to implement echo events so that the stick can be moved in a direction once and the value changes continuously over time (after waiting for a certain duration to pass).

I poorly express myself, I mean by exception, directly handling `InputEventJoypadMotion` as their own type on action inside the slider. Instead of behing managed by `p_event->is_action_pressed("ui_up", true)` should we check the `get_action_strength` when we handle a  `InputEventJoypadMotion`.

I not really familiar with the basecode so maybe there is a better solution to fix this behavior.

Maybe it's a bit too much but, what about introducing an _InputEvent::is_action_held_ method with a delay parameter?
And then, gui components could optionally switch between _is_action_pressed_ and _is_action_held_

I did a first quickfix based on what has been done in `Viewport.cpp`. Seems to work fine but I need to test further before creating a PR. 

I would also like to improve the whole behavior, but I'm not sure if I should do it right now or create a proposal (Could @Calinou help my on this one, thanks) ?
- If we quickly move the axis to the left or right, it should only increment by one step
- If we held the stick to the left or right, it should increment the step until we unheld the stick (could be easier for user with motion issue)

> I would also like to improve the whole behavior, but I'm not sure if I should do it right now or create a proposal

It's probably a good idea to create a proposal for this.
**Edit:** Proposal opened: https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/4911

Ideally, sliders should behave like this with both keyboard and gamepad input. Thanks to the operating system, keyboards will automatically provide echo events, but gamepads don't provide echo events for their buttons or axes. Therefore, this behavior needs to be manually implemented for gamepad input.

I suggest using a delay of 0.5 seconds and a repeat rate of 20 repeats/second, similar to Windows' default rate for repeating keyboard input. This delay and repeat rate should be adjustable with project settings for accessibility reasons as well.

Here in QuakeSpasm-Spiked, I'm pressing the left/right keys a few times then holding the left or right key for a while:

https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/180032/179607977-b3036deb-0fb7-4962-8824-a5063abee7e7.mp4

Hello, it would be great to have an is_echo() function for gamepads, which would avoid this issue. Reproducing this in GDscript with timers in each interface code is feasible but generates a lot of unnecessary code.  This solution would enable gamedevs to use the function when needed (UI) and leave it be when not needed (gameplay).

> Hello, it would be great to have an is_echo() function for gamepads, which would avoid this issue. 

Gamepads never send echo inputs, so `is_echo()` would be invalid. Only keyboards send echo events as determined by the operating system configuration.

Instead, we should look into properly handling analog stick UI inputs out of the box (D-pad input should also send those echo events for consistency). This is entirely feasible, but requires manually implementing echo inputs in certain UI nodes (such as Slider and SpinBox).

I tried and add the same behavior to every node (slider, popup menu, item list, tree etc) but it seems more like a workaround (it is also my first PR so my lack of experience in c++ and Godot source code could be the real issue). 

Even if a gamepad doesn't have an echo, could we implement a behavior inside Input to re-trigger an event. maybe for an UI exclusive mode? 

Or we could list witch component to prioritize like the slider and popup menu and add the echoing

I understand that "Gamepads never send echo inputs, so is_echo() would be invalid" -> my point is that as a gamedev I need an is_echo() function (or equivalent) for gamepads in order to detect repeated input signals in certain situations (mainly UI). I can reproduce it with a timer in GDscript (blocking input repetition happening within a given short time frame) but it is tedious and ridiculous to reproduce for every game UI. Currently porting an interface game to Switch, I realize how important this is and if Godot is to be used for console games, where all navigation happens with the stick, this issue is a real problem.

Are we sure that all Controls handle analog input correctly?
I still pretty new to Godot Engine's code, but since we check with ui_XXX, should the alt key take the lead if the analog isn't set?

What I mean is that this PR adds a specific logic to two nodes just to handle analog input, so I wonder if all other controls can handle it. If not, including axis in default controls can lead to exposing buggy behavior.

We got a [discussion]( https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/63168#issuecomment-1419268885) about it and I ended up doing a per control implementation since the behavoir of some control node can be quite different from one to another.

That's why I targetted pop_menu and slider, the most common control that should be usable with a gamepad. 

Of course, there is maybe a solution to add it to all control by I'm certainly too inexperienced with the engine to find that solution.

Adding it to other Controls would involve testing all of them and tweaking the behavior where necessary.
Good point about commonly used Controls, Tree for example is not used in games at all, so there is no point in fixing it. So I think this PR is enough to cover the most common use-cases.
